symptom.disease_name: Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

sampled_features.disease_name: Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features

additional_requirements: delusions_and_hallucinations occur exclusively during the manic episode

S019.name: Delusions
S019.description: Fixed beliefs that do not change easily, even in the face of contradictory evidence.

subtypes.Persecutory Delusions: The false belief that one is being harmed or monitored by other people or organizations.
subtypes.Referential Delusions: The conviction that ordinary events, remarks, or behaviors have specific relevance to oneself.
subtypes.Grandiose Delusions: The false belief that one possesses special abilities, power, or fame.
subtypes.Erotomanic Delusions: The false belief that another person is in love with or has affection for them.
subtypes.Nihilistic Delusions: A destructive or negative conviction that the world is ending or that a major catastrophe will occur.
subtypes.Somatic Delusions: The baseless conviction that there is a serious abnormality with one's body or organs.
subtypes.Jealous Delusions: The conviction that one's spouse or romantic partner is being unfaithful without sufficient evidence.

S020.name: Hallucinations
S020.description: Perception-like experiences that occur without an external stimulus and are as vivid and clear as normal perception.

subtypes.Auditory Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of hearing voices or sounds when there is no actual sound.
subtypes.Visual Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of seeing people or objects that do not exist.
subtypes.Tactile Hallucinations: Experiencing the sensation of being touched or movement on the skin when there is no actual stimulus.
subtypes.Olfactory Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of smelling odors that do not exist.
subtypes.Gustatory Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of tasting flavors that are not actually present.

S033.name: Elevated_Irritable_Mood
S033.description: A distinct period of abnormally and persistently elevated, expansive, or irritable mood.

subtypes.Elevated Mood: A mood that is abnormally high, euphoric, and full of unmotivated happiness and vitality.
subtypes.Irritable Mood: A state where one gets angry or aggressive even at minor stimuli.
subtypes.Mood Lability: Rapid shifts in mood, alternating unpredictably between euphoria and irritability.

S034.name: Increased_Activity
S034.description: Abnormally and persistently increased goal-directed activity or energy.

subtypes.Increased Energy: Overflowing physical and mental energy, leading to an inability to stay still and a desire to keep moving.
subtypes.Hyperactivity: Doing far more work than usual or starting multiple activities simultaneously.
subtypes.Psychomotor Agitation: Inability to tolerate resting or stopping, driven by a constant need to do something.

S037.name: Pressured_Speech
S037.description: More talkative than usual or pressure to keep talking.

subtypes.Talkativeness: Speaking far more than usual and continuing to talk without rest.
subtypes.Rapid Speech: Speech speed is so fast that it is difficult for others to understand or interrupt.
subtypes.Pressured Speech: Cannot stop talking or tolerate silence due to an internal pressure to keep speaking.

S038.name: Racing_Thoughts
S038.description: Flight of ideas or subjective experience that thoughts are racing.

subtypes.Racing Thoughts: Thoughts spinning too fast in the head, constantly jumping from one idea to another.
subtypes.Flooding of Thoughts: Too many thoughts emerging simultaneously, making them disorganized.
subtypes.Inability to Control Thoughts: Unable to stop or slow down thoughts and unable to calm the mind.

S040.name: Increased_Goal_Activity
S040.description: Increase in goal-directed activity (at work, school, socially, or sexually) or purposeless psychomotor agitation.

subtypes.Occupational Hyperactivity: Driving significantly more projects or work than usual in the workplace or academic setting.
subtypes.Social Hyperactivity: Becoming much more sociable and extroverted than usual, actively meeting and contacting people.
subtypes.Hypersexuality: Significantly increased interest in or activity regarding sex.
subtypes.Psychomotor Agitation: Purposeless non-goal-directed activity, such as pacing or hand-wringing, driven by an inability to sit still.

symptom.disease_info: Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features is characterized by at least one full manic episode, often with marked functional impairment, that may be accompanied by delusions or hallucinations congruent or incongruent with mood. Episodes typically develop over days to weeks and can last weeks to months, with intervening periods of partial or full remission; depressive episodes are common but not required for diagnosis. Psychotic features usually emerge at the more severe end of mania or depression and help distinguish Bipolar I from Bipolar II and cyclothymia, as well as from primary psychotic disorders like schizophrenia where mood symptoms are not as prominent or temporally linked. The course is often recurrent, influenced by stress, sleep disruption, and biological vulnerability, and may be complicated by impaired insight, risky behavior, and strained social and occupational functioning.

patient.stressor: In the months leading up to her episode, Eunhae had been picking up extra shifts at the long‑term care facility due to staffing shortages while also coordinating medical appointments and translation for her aging parents, one of whom had a recent minor stroke. Her previously structured routine of early‑morning tai chi, careful budgeting, and quiet evenings gradually gave way to fragmented sleep and a sense of responsibility that she had to personally safeguard every detail of her patients’ and parents’ care. Over roughly two months she became increasingly overextended at work and at home, insisting on taking on more tasks and clashing with colleagues and family when they questioned her decisions, which led to noticeable strain in her marriage and complaints from coworkers about her behavior. The situation became clinically significant when she began insisting she alone could prevent serious harm to her patients and parents, refused to leave work or sleep, and her husband and charge nurse brought her to the emergency department after she confronted a physician and tried to override medical orders.
patient.chief_complaint: “I can’t slow down—I have too many important things to take care of and I feel driven to keep doing more, day and night.”

S019.name: Delusions
S019.description: Fixed beliefs that do not change easily, even in the face of contradictory evidence.
S019.manifestation: Lately I’ve been completely convinced that if I’m not watching every chart and every pill, the doctors and nurses will miss something and my patients or my parents will die, and no matter how many times people tell me everything is fine, I just know in my gut that only I can catch the mistakes and prevent a disaster.

S020.name: Hallucinations
S020.description: Perception-like experiences that occur without an external stimulus and are as vivid and clear as normal perception.
S020.manifestation: When I’m walking down the hallway at the facility or trying to lie down at home, I keep hearing a man’s voice right behind my ear saying things like, “Don’t sleep, they’re counting on you,” or calling my name, even when I can see there’s nobody there.

S033.name: Elevated_Irritable_Mood
S033.description: A distinct period of abnormally and persistently elevated, expansive, or irritable mood.
S033.manifestation: Most of the time I feel cranked up and on edge, like I’m running on electricity—one minute I’m overly cheerful and telling everyone how amazing I am at keeping everyone safe, and the next I snap at my husband or coworkers over the smallest question because it feels like they’re getting in the way of something urgent.

S034.name: Increased_Activity
S034.description: Abnormally and persistently increased goal-directed activity or energy.
S034.manifestation: From the moment I wake up, I’m pacing, cleaning, checking meds, calling doctors, writing lists, and I literally can’t sit through a meal or a TV show because it feels unbearable to stop moving when there’s always one more thing I could be doing.

S037.name: Pressured_Speech
S037.description: More talkative than usual or pressure to keep talking.
S037.manifestation: My husband and coworkers keep telling me I’m talking a mile a minute, jumping from my parents’ appointments to new protocols we should use at work to ideas about starting my own care agency, and I feel like if I pause for even a second, all these important thoughts will explode out of my head, so I just keep talking over everyone.

S038.name: Racing_Thoughts
S038.description: Flight of ideas or subjective experience that thoughts are racing.
S038.manifestation: My mind is going so fast that as soon as I start thinking about one thing—like my mom’s blood pressure—it instantly skips to reorganizing the whole med cart, then to fixing the schedule for the night shift, then to calling my sister, all at the same time, and I can’t slow it down enough to finish a single thought.

S040.name: Increased_Goal_Activity
S040.description: Increase in goal-directed activity (at work, school, socially, or sexually) or purposeless psychomotor agitation.
S040.manifestation: For weeks I’ve been taking extra shifts, staying up all night rewriting care plans, rearranging my parents’ medication schedules, emailing administrators with “improvement plans,” and even when my body feels exhausted I feel this relentless push, like I’ll be failing everyone if I don’t keep doing more and more.
